rows.label: Terminal benefits exempt up to 25% of basic salary earned
rows.value: Gratuities, contract gratuities and severance pay are exempt up to 25% of the basic salary earned during the period of employment; the excess is taxed at the marginal rates.

rows.label: PAYE: employer deducts monthly and remits by the 15th of the following month
rows.value: Employers calculate PAYE on each employee's monthly earnings (20% up to M6,480, 30% above, less the M1,020 credit), withhold it and remit it to the RSL by the 15th of the following month. Example: M10,000 a month → M2,352 − M1,020 = M1,332.

sections.title: Dividends, interest and payments to non-residents

rows.label: Non-residents: dividends
rows.note: Lesotho-source dividends paid to non-residents (none on dividends out of manufacturing income; 10% or 15% under the RSA and UK treaties). Under review: from the RSL Withholding Tax Guide dated April 2010 (still the guide the RSL withholding tax page links); a later rate change was not checked on an official page.

source.title: Withholding Tax Guide (April 2010)

rows.label: Non-residents: interest
rows.note: Lesotho-source interest paid to non-residents (10% under the RSA and UK treaties). Under review: from the RSL Withholding Tax Guide dated April 2010 (still the guide the RSL withholding tax page links); a later rate change was not checked on an official page.

source.title: Withholding Tax Guide (April 2010)

rows.label: Non-residents: royalties, natural resource payments and management fees
rows.note: Lesotho-source royalties, natural resource payments and management fees paid to non-residents (15% on royalties for technology producing manufacturing income; 10% under the RSA and UK treaties). Under review: from the RSL Withholding Tax Guide dated April 2010 (still the guide the RSL withholding tax page links); a later rate change was not checked on an official page.

source.title: Withholding Tax Guide (April 2010)

rows.label: Non-residents: services, artistes, entertainers and sportspersons

sections.title: Freelancers, contractors and the self-employed

rows.label: Resident contractors: 5% withholding
rows.note: payments to resident contractors (leasing of vehicles, plant or equipment, construction, transport, painting, plumbing, roofing, earthmoving, landscaping, installation and similar); not for an individual's principal residence. Under review: from the RSL Withholding Tax Guide dated April 2010 (still the guide the RSL withholding tax page links); a later rate change was not checked on an official page.

source.title: Withholding Tax Guide (April 2010)

rows.label: Resident contractors: no withholding on fees under M3,000
rows.note: total fee payable to a resident contractor. Under review: from the RSL Withholding Tax Guide dated April 2010 (still the guide the RSL withholding tax page links); a later rate change was not checked on an official page.

source.title: Withholding Tax Guide (April 2010)

rows.label: Withholding on services from resident and non-resident suppliers, on the amount before VAT
rows.value: Payers withhold tax from the gross amount (before VAT) payable for services, from resident and non-resident suppliers, and remit it monthly; the payee accounts for it on the annual income tax return.

source.title: Withholding Tax

rows.label: Sole traders: provisional tax in quarterly instalments
rows.value: Individuals with business income (sole traders, partners) pay provisional tax ahead of the year end, usually in three quarterly instalments, and file an annual return.
